title: Evaluation case
description: One element of eval/cases/{train,test_seen,test_unseen}.json. The two-channel envelope is dictated by MLflow's optimize_prompts, not chosen: `inputs` carries everything predict_fn needs and `expectations` everything a scorer needs, and there is no third place to put anything (agent_architecture.md 6.1, findings.md 'Optimizer internals'). Cases are emitted by the generator and never hand-edited.

tool_name.description: The registered names a root-agent trajectory can contain (agent_architecture.md 0). `query_database_tool` is the sub-agent's inner tool and never appears here.

card_id.description: The eleven reference cards, identical to lookup_reference's `topic` enum (agent_architecture.md 3.2).

unit.description: The answer contract's unit vocabulary. `L` and `mm` are one quantity on the lysimeter columns and `%` and `%θ` are one unit; nothing else converts (agent_architecture.md 7).

question.description: The paraphrase the agent is shown, EN or DE. Roofs are named in the agent's vocabulary or in alias-covered natural language, never by raw column name.

as_of.description: The scenario clock, an instant in the site's own offset-bearing form. A numeric offset is required and `Z` is not accepted: the stamp must name the Berlin day the case is about, and the conversion to UTC belongs to connect_asof, never to the caller (decisions.md 'The as-of cut').

case_id.description: Template id plus a zero-padded instance number, e.g. T09-0142. Cases are sorted by this field in the emitted array.

template_id.description: The catalog template this case instantiates. The unit of analysis for every aggregate and the resampling unit of the paired bootstrap (agent_architecture.md 7).

params.description: The sampled parameter values, one key per parameter the template declares. Carried so a case is reproducible from its template and so per-param disjointness between train and test_seen is checkable after the fact.

language.description: Reported as a stratum: DE routing accuracy is a measured quantity, not sampling noise (questions.md 1.7).

status.description: The agent's contract status, two-valued and NOT the tool-level outcome enum of section 3. A tool's `not_available` is the upstream cause that can make this correct, not the thing measured.

answer.description: The materialized oracle answer: a boolean, a number, an ISO date, or null. Null covers an abstention and a plot deliverable alike.

answer_metric.description: `skipped` marks the answer metric legitimately undefined for this case; the aggregation callable turns it into a skip with coverage reported, never into a 0 (agent_architecture.md 7).

expected_tool_calls.description: The gold trajectory. Keeps ADK's own key name, which keeps MLflow's ADK ToolTrajectory scorer available as a cross-check. Calls beyond this set cost nothing.

must_not_tools.description: The listed distractors, and the only route errors that score. An unlisted call is free (decisions.md 'Trajectory scoring and routing probes').

gold_cards.description: Cards the run should have retrieved, scored as recall over the union of every lookup_reference call. Non-empty implies a lookup call in the gold trajectory — see the validator below.

argument_checks.description: Declarative conjuncts over tool ARGUMENTS, so the scorer never branches per template and never reads a tool result.

allOf.title: A numeric answer carries the tolerance it is compared under

tolerance.description: How the answer metric compares. `exact` takes no value; `abs` and `rel` require one (`rel` as a fraction, so 2 % is 0.02).

args.description: Illustrative arguments. Scoring reads `argument_checks`, not this object: trajectory is binary over tool names plus those checks, never an argument-exact match.

path.description: Dotted path into one call's argument object, e.g. `forcings.precip.2026-03-15` or `series.0.source`. It addresses arguments only; there is no path into a tool result.

op.description: `eq` exact match; `set_eq` a set match, for a series selection whose order carries no meaning; `present` a candidate-chosen value that must merely exist and be plausible.

value.description: The expected value for `eq` / `set_eq`. Absent for `present`.

resolve.description: `window` normalizes the agent's argument through the same layer-1 window resolver the tool uses, against inputs.as_of, before comparing — so a candidate that wrote a relative window scores identically to one that wrote the dates. This is a property of the value, which is why it is a flag rather than a fourth `op` (decisions.md 'Plotting').

plausible.description: Bounds for `present`: the value must exist and fall inside them. Carries the counterfactual families, whose arguments are scored on presence and plausibility and never on the tool result.

pins.description: The surface this answer was materialized against, stamped per case (agent_architecture.md 6.1). A case whose pins no longer match the run's is not comparable to one that does.

gr2l_canary.description: The committed GR2L request/response canary hash, present exactly where the oracle called the service.

station_derivation.description: Version of the station derivation — the per-field aggregation, the day boundary, the sentinel filter — which the database hash does not cover.

weather_source.description: The provenance each weather window resolved to while materializing the answer. Empty where no weather was read; two entries where the case made two calls that resolved differently.
